evidence.note: Recognized that incremental sed-patching had corrupted parser/sema/codegen and switched approach to clean full-file rewrites — a genuine correction when the editing method was falsified, though the churn was largely self-inflicted.

Diagnosed that the lexer's newline-skipping design broke the preprocessor's directive detection and made a real representational change (added Token::Newline, changed lexer to emit newlines, parser to skip them) — adapting the design to fit a needed feature.

Repeatedly identified 'incomplete type information' as the recurring root cause behind nested ->/struct member failures, and at 431/433 attempted a resolve() fix; at 436 noted it 'apparently didn't help' — root-cause diagnosis present but the response stayed a patch rather than a redesign of the type representation.
Many full codegen.rs rewrites; several driven by sed-corruption recovery rather than design pivots, showing significant churn and a foundation that plateaued at ~277-294/780.

Detected a regression (294→277), forced a clean rebuild to verify build integrity, and reasoned about whether recent parser edits caused it — evidence of reconciling design with reality, but corrective action remained localized bug-patching.

reasoning: The agent clearly diagnoses root causes behind clusters of failures (newline handling, register widths, incomplete type info) and does refactor affected areas when a feature doesn't fit — matching the level-5 anchor and touching level-8 diagnostic behavior. However, when it identified the central structural limitation (no real type representation for structs/nested members) it applied an ineffective patch rather than the targeted redesign (proper type info / IR) that level 8 describes, and much of its 'adaptation' was rewrite churn to recover from its own sed corruption. This places it solidly at the mid anchor rather than higher.
